## What you did
- Shipped SAML assertion signature verification for Fernhill's Okta in PR #418: signxml verifies the signature on the assertion (not the response) against per-tenant IdP certificates (migration 0142), SHA-256 and above only — you refused the legacy SHA-1 flag — plus replay protection rejecting a repeated assertion ID [2].
- Fixed the flaky `test_acs_rejects_expired_assertion`: the 3-second clock skew made the 2-second expiry margin timing-dependent, so you froze time with freezegun instead of sleeping, and converted the two other sleeping tests [1].
- Cleaned up `kestrel/auth` for ruff 0.8 and mypy (a missing Issuer/Subject is now a 401 validation error, not a 500), and split the 900-line `saml_utils.py` into a `saml/` package — assertions, metadata, bindings — behind a shim so old imports keep working; full suite green, lint and types clean [1].

## What changed
- Maya approved #418 (one non-blocking nit on an error message) and merged it on 17 Nov; it goes out with that night's staging deploy, so signature validation is on staging ahead of the Wednesday EOD deadline [3].
- Tom requested changes on your cleanup PR #423: split the `saml/` module move from the lint fixes, since the 1,900-line diff hides the real changes — he said he'd approve both PRs the same day [4].

## What is still open
- Fernhill end-to-end SSO walkthrough on staging, Thursday 10am NY with their Okta tenant; Priya runs the demo, you just need to be on the call — unblocked by the #418 merge [1][3].
- Split #423 into two PRs (module move vs lint fixes) as Tom asked [4].
- Move the replay cache off the per-process TTLCache to Redis (SET NX EX keyed by tenant + assertion ID, TTL = NotOnOrAfter + skew) before production — it was on your list for today [1][2].
